title: Show the decades side by side
brief: I want students to see how our town's rainfall and temperature have shifted decade by decade without me exporting charts by hand.

target_population.role: secondary-school geography teacher building lesson material from local records
target_population.coverage_limit: a fixed fictional archive of three stations and forty years; no live or real data

core_task.summary: compare two decades of rainfall at one station and read the anomaly note
core_task.success_oracle: selecting station Kerrbrook Weir with decades 1990s and 2010s renders both series and an annotation naming 2017 the driest year in the archive

not_applicable_states.loading: the forty-year archive is bundled local JSON parsed at startup, so chart composition happens synchronously with no fetch to wait on
not_applicable_states.empty: the explorer ships a fixed seeded archive covering every station and decade its pickers can express, so a no-data result is unreachable by construction
not_applicable_states.validation-error: every input is a constrained picker over the seeded archive; there is no free-form field whose value could be rejected

state_recipes.success: pick Kerrbrook Weir, decades 1990s and 2010s, and compare; the paired series render with the 2017 annotation
state_recipes.focus: press Tab from page load until the station picker shows its visible focus ring
state_recipes.mobile: load the explorer at 390x844; the chart reflows beneath the stacked pickers

acceptance_facts: The seeded archive holds forty years of monthly rainfall and temperature for three invented stations.
Comparing the 1990s against the 2010s at Kerrbrook Weir annotates 2017 as the driest year in the archive.
Every chart states the fictional dataset name and the decade range directly on the figure.

product_signature.mechanism: decade-pair comparator that overlays two eras of a single station
product_signature.anchor: paired-series chart filling the main stage
product_signature.brief_trace: shifted decade by decade without me exporting charts by hand
product_signature.counterfactual: a single-series weather dashboard would satisfy a display brief but cannot put one era against another
product_signature.task_proof: success capture shows both decade series overlaid with the 2017 driest-year annotation

anti_goals: no live weather feeds, APIs, or real station data
no climate forecasting or policy claims; the archive is explicitly fictional teaching data
no user data entry; the explorer is strictly read-only

content_seed.data_notes: all station names and forty years of monthly values are invented; anomalies are planted so annotations are deterministic
